Rowan has a Quartz feature record whose stored value is 'high', so an equals-high predicate would return true. Mica has a Quartz feature record whose stored value is 'low', so an equals-high predicate would return false. The candidate instead uses operator 'present'. Under the stipulated literal semantics, 'present' asks only whether a Quartz feature record exists and ignores its stored value. A Quartz record exists for Rowan, so the candidate operator returns true for Rowan; a Quartz record also exists for Mica, so it returns true for Mica. Thus the candidate produces true/true rather than the source-required true/false contrast. The matching prose statement does not repair the discriminator's operator semantics.
